narrative.overview:
The page is a sheet of white paper, not a card sitting on a grey board. Content sits directly on it: a semibold page title, a quiet meta line, one row of filters, then rows of records. Sections are a 16px heading over a single hairline, not boxed cards nested in boxed cards. Facts on a detail page read as Notion property rows: a grey label column, an ink value column, and no table borders. The sidebar is a slightly warmer paper (#f7f7f5) separated by a hairline, never a navy rail.

Colour is rationed. Everything is warm ink on white; the one accent blue is reserved for primary actions, links, focus and selection. State is carried by nine borderless pastel tones in sentence case, and company identity by a small square monogram tile in its own pastel tone, so a company never reads as one more status. Depth is near-zero: hairlines separate surfaces at rest, and only floating layers (menus, popovers, dialogs, the sticky phone nav) lift off the page.

The system is built inside Ant Design 5 through theme tokens (`antTheme.ts`), a global surface layer (`notion.css`) that reaches what tokens cannot, and three primitives (Pill, PageHeader, PropertyList). Density is a working back office: 14px body, 32px controls, 30px menu items, 34px property rows. It is used as often on a phone in the field as at a desk.

**Coverage boundary.** The system is fully applied only to the app shell, the global theme, Water Mitigation list and detail (including the Photos, Scope and Report tabs and the shared FileGallery), Estimate Creation, the Repair Estimate Wizard, and Supplements list and detail (`/supplements`). Supplement status tones live in one map (`components/supplement/supplementUi.tsx`: Identified orange, In progress blue, Submitted purple, Under review yellow, Approved green, Denied red, Withdrawn gray); supplement-only surface classes are the `sup-*` block at the end of `notion.css`. The Work Orders list (`/work-orders`, hidden from the menus for now while the todo board takes the home page; its routes remain) is on the system too: its status tones live in `components/work-order/workOrderUi.tsx` (Draft gray, Pending approval orange, Approved purple, In progress blue, Completed green, Cancelled red, On hold yellow), it shares the status view tabs (`ui-status-tabs`) and table meta line (`ui-cell-meta`) with Supplements, and its own classes are the `wo-*` block; the work order detail and creation pages are not migrated yet. The Rebuild project detail modal (`/rebuild-projects`) is on the system: property rows and a completion-document checklist beside the claim's latest insurance estimate PDF in a frame (phones get one column and open PDFs in a new tab); its status tones live in `components/rebuild/rebuildUi.tsx` (Pending orange, Assigned blue, In progress purple, Completed green, Invoiced yellow, Docs sent pink, Closed gray) and its classes are the `rb-*` block in `components/rebuild/rebuild.css`. The Rebuild list is on the system too: a PageHeader, its totals as plain figures on the sheet (label over a 20px ink value, two by two on phones, no cards), the shared status view tabs, a table on desktop and the phone row list below 768px; its create, edit, contractor, upload, Generate Document and Photos to PDF dialogs open as phone sheets. The WM Sketch tab inherits the theme only: its tool and legend colours mirror the canvas and the exported PDF, so they are deliberately left as they are. The Claim Follow-up claim page (`/claim-followup/claim/:id`) is on the system, with the pieces it shares with the follow-up list: the estimates panel, the Resolve form and the communication history (`components/claim-followup/`). Its stage track and task status tones come from one module (`claimProgress.ts`: Pending blue, Awaiting response orange, Awaiting confirmation purple, Responded yellow, Resolved green, Cancelled gray), and its surface classes are the `fu-*` block at the end of `notion.css`. The page runs on the Comfort scale (see Typography). Its email composer (`EmailComposer.tsx`, shared with the follow-up list, the task email page and the client page) is a sheet of mail rows (Regarding, From, To, Cc, Subject: grey label column, borderless controls, hairline between rows), then the body editor, then Send in a footer; templates and AI drafts are one menu button each, never a row of buttons. Email templates are managed in a drawer (`EmailTemplateManager.tsx`: list on a Sidebar Paper pane, editor beside it, one pane at a time on phones) whose claim fields are `{{placeholders}}` from `emailTemplates.ts`; a field with no value stays highlighted in yellow and sending with one asks first. The follow-up list itself keeps its own inline `cf-*` styles and is only partly migrated. The signed-out pages (sign in, forgot password, reset password) share `components/auth/AuthLayout.tsx`: the workspace mark at 24px in the top-left corner and one 360px column directly on white, no card and no shadow, with visible labels above `large` controls, a "Forgot password?" link in the password label row, errors in the red tag tone without a border, and result states (email sent, invalid link, password updated) as a title, a line and full-width buttons in the same column; its classes are the `auth-*` block in `components/auth/AuthLayout.css`. The Client detail page (`/clients/:id`) is on the system: the client's facts as two property columns under the PageHeader, tabs straight on the sheet with quiet counts, and claims as hairline rows (`ui-collapse-rows`: claim number, status pill, a grey insurer · loss · RCV line). An open claim puts the work (negotiation history, contracts, email with Sent / Received view tabs, todos beside notes, completion photos) in a wide column and the claim's facts, jobs and document counts and activity in a 340px column beside it, one column below 1200px with the facts first. Its sections are `ClaimSection` (`components/client/ClaimSection.tsx`: a 14px heading over a hairline with text-button actions; `size="page"` for 16px tab sections), Financials shows payments and profitability as figures on the sheet (label over an ink value) and the Document Hub filters by type with filter chips; its classes are the `cl-*` block in `notion.css`. The Todos board (`/todos`, the home page that replaced the dashboard) is on the system: each person's own board, three columns of flat hairline cards (To do gray, In progress blue, Done green, one map in `components/todo/todoUi.tsx`) dragged to set priority, each led by a status circle (an empty ring, a half-filled ring, a check) that steps the todo to the next column. Desktop opens a card in place to edit it; phones get the status view tabs over a full-bleed row list with a drag handle per row and edit in a sheet. Done shows the latest ten until asked for the rest. The same todos list on the client page inside each claim (with the client's general todos and, for someone else's, the owner's name), using the same circle. Its classes are the `td-*` block in `components/todo/todo.css`. About 80 other pages inherit only the theme tokens and the global tag, table and card overrides; they still contain hardcoded legacy antd hex colours and inline styles. Treat those pages as unmigrated, not as precedent.
keyCharacteristics: White page, warm-grey sidebar, hairline (#e9e9e7) separation, no shadow at rest.
One accent blue for actions, links, focus and selection; money and totals stay ink.
Nine borderless pastel tag pairs, sentence case, 4px radius, 12px/500.
Company identity as a square pastel monogram tile, never a pill.
Property rows (grey label, ink value, no borders) for detail facts.
System sans throughout, 14px body, 24px semibold page titles.
Phone-first affordances: 52px top bar, 56px bottom nav, single-column row list.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Blue means "you can act here" or "this is selected". Totals, amounts and record titles stay ink, however important they are.

rules.name: The Same Key, Same Tone Rule
rules.body: A value that has a colour gets it from a fixed map (status) or from a stable hash of its id (companies, `toneFromKey`), so it reads the same colour on every page. The hash draws from seven tones and skips gray (reads as empty) and red (reads as an error).

rules.name: The Sentence Case Rule
rules.body: Statuses and labels are humanized to sentence case ("Awaiting response", not "AWAITING_RESPONSE"); `humanize()` exists for raw enum values. Uppercase appears only where the data itself is a code, such as a company's short code in its monogram.

rules.name: The Grey Label Rule
rules.body: Labels are regular weight (400) in Label Grey; values are ink. Weight never distinguishes a label from its value.

rules.name: The Only Floaters Cast Shadows Rule
rules.body: If it sits on the page, it is flat with a hairline. If it floats above the page, it gets the Elevated shadow. Nothing in between.

dos: Do put content directly on the white page; use a 16px/600 heading over a 1px hairline (#e9e9e7) to start a section.
Do show detail facts as property rows: grey 400 label column (160px desktop, 136px phone), ink value column, no borders, "Empty" for missing values.
Do use the Pill primitive with one of the nine tones for any value that carries state, in sentence case, and take its tone from a fixed map or `toneFromKey`.
Do show a company as its square monogram tile, toned by its id.
Do reserve Ledger Blue (#1f74c9) for primary actions, links, focus and selection; keep amounts and totals in ink.
Do use the PageHeader primitive: 24px/600 title (22px on phones), 13px grey meta line, actions on the right that wrap below on phones.
Do give only floating layers (menus, popovers, pickers, modals) the Elevated shadow.
Do take colours from `tokens.ts` / `tokens.css` variables instead of hex literals when migrating a page.
donts: Don't wrap page sections in bordered, shadowed cards, or nest cards inside cards.
Don't use a dark or navy sidebar, or a blue active bar on navigation; selection is an ink wash.
Don't give tags borders, saturated antd colours, or ALL-CAPS enum text.
Don't render a company as a pill, or use gray or red for a company tone.
Don't colour money, totals or record titles blue.
Don't set readable text in Faint Glyph (#a5a29a); it is for decorative icons only.
Don't treat unmigrated pages (the follow-up list and the roughly 80 legacy pages) as precedent for colour or spacing.
